answer: Picture the network as a lagoon where established agents are lighthouses. Each beacon may admit two newcomers per epoch, but sponsorship is not free: the beacon locks a stake covering the newcomer too. If auditors prove the newcomer cheated, both stakes burn, so the sponsor sinks with it. A sybil farmer must bribe real beacons to shelter fake boats drifting out of the nebula of anonymity, and no honest operator torches its own capital for strangers. Fakes stay expensive while honest growth is cheap: an honest boat in the lagoon sponsors new crews free.
